strings.name: José Ramos-Horta
strings.summary: Ramos-Horta campaigned abroad for Timorese self-determination and shared the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with Bishop Belo. After independence he served as foreign minister, prime minister and president, survived an assassination attempt and worked in UN peacebuilding. Returning to the presidency in 2022, he continued using diplomacy and international cooperation to support governance and regional integration, including ASEAN membership.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Long promoted Timor-Leste’s independence and international diplomacy, won the Nobel Peace Prize and contributes to the new state’s institutions and governance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Dili, Timor-Leste, then a Portuguese colony.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied international and human-rights law in The Hague and Strasbourg; peace-studies master’s at Antioch (1984).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Self-determination diplomacy
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advocated Timorese self-determination internationally and at the UN, sharing the 1996 peace prize with Belo.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Post-independence governance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Held senior offices in the new state and participated in UN peacebuilding and regional cooperation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Witnessed ASEAN accession
strings.timeline.t1.text: Attended Timor-Leste’s formal admission as ASEAN’s eleventh member.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Returned to presidency
strings.timeline.t2.text: Began a second presidential tenure after winning election.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Led UN peacebuilding mission
strings.timeline.t3.text: Headed the UN integrated peacebuilding office in Guinea-Bissau.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Survived assassination attempt
strings.timeline.t4.text: Seriously wounded in a shooting, later returning to presidential duties after treatment.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became president
strings.timeline.t5.text: Elected president, serving the first tenure until 2012.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became prime minister
strings.timeline.t6.text: Took over as prime minister during a political crisis.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Served as foreign minister
strings.timeline.t7.text: Served as foreign minister after Timor-Leste restored independence.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Shared Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t8.text: Shared the prize with Carlos Belo for efforts toward a peaceful solution in Timor-Leste.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Completed peace-studies master’s
strings.timeline.t9.text: Completed Antioch master’s studies emphasizing international law and international relations.
strings.timeline.t10.title: Began overseas diplomacy
strings.timeline.t10.text: Left Timor-Leste to seek UN support and represented self-determination abroad.
